keyVerseText: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun יָרֵךְ (yârêk) derives from an unused root meaning 'to be soft,' which highlights its connection to the fleshy, tender parts of the body. This etymological nuance enriches the common English glosses such as 'thigh' or 'side' by emphasizing the physical softness and vulnerability of this area, often associated with strength and life-giving power. The term thus carries both a literal anatomical sense and a figurative dimension tied to vital bodily regions.
usageInScripture: The word יָרֵךְ appears 34 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently translated in contexts referring to the 'thigh,' 'side,' or 'loin.' Its usage ranges from the literal fleshly part of the body—such as the outside of the thigh where a sword was worn—to euphemistic references to generative organs, reflecting its role as the seat of procreative power. The top translations like 'on the side,' 'thigh,' and 'under my thigh' reveal a stable semantic field centered on the physical and symbolic significance of this body region.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding יָרֵךְ as the tender, vital part of the body enriches our grasp of biblical imagery related to covenant, authority, and human life. The thigh, as the place where a sword was girded, symbolizes strength and readiness, while its connection to procreative power points to God's design for life and blessing. This dual physical and symbolic meaning invites believers to appreciate how God engages with the whole person—body and soul—in covenant relationships, calling us to faithfulness and life-giving obedience rooted in His power and grace.
keyVerseReflection: In Genesis 24:2, Abraham commands his servant, 'Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh,' a phrase that invokes the intimate and solemn nature of the oath being made. The word יָרֵךְ here underscores the seriousness of the covenant act, as placing a hand under the thigh symbolizes placing oneself under the authority and life-giving power associated with this part of the body. This act reflects a deep trust and commitment before God, highlighting the sacredness of promises made in His presence.
